newsitem.title: USA: Government slams FBI lab in Oklahoma bombing - Paper.
newsitem.headline: Government slams FBI lab in Oklahoma bombing - Paper.

text.p: The FBI crime laboratory submitted flawed conclusions in its investigation of the fatal bombing of the Oklahoma City federal building two years ago, Justice Department office found in a draft report obtained by the Los Angeles Times.
The bombing took 168 lives and injured 850 people.

"The draft report shows that FBI examiners could not identify the triggering device for the truck bomb or how it was detonated on April 19, 1995, and it warns that a poorly maintained lab environment could have led to contamination of critical pieces of evidence, such as debris found on the clothing of defendant Tomothy J. McVeigh," the Times reported in Saturday editions.

The inspector general's office of the Justice Department found conclusions of the laboratory "scientifically unsound" and "biased in favour of the prosecution," the newspaper said in a report from Washington.

McVeigh's trial was scheduled to begin March 31 in Denver, where it was moved after attorneys said pre-trial publicity prevented a fair trial for McVeigh and co-defendant Terry Nichols anywhere in Oklahoma. Nichols was to be tried later.

"If entered into evidence at McVeigh's trial, scheduled to begin March 31, the draft report could provide a measure of doubt about whether bomb residue evidence was properly handled and professionally examined by experts at the Washington lab. Forensic evidence is an important element of the government's largely circumstantial case...," the Times reported.
The FBI refused comment until the report was in its final form, the newspaper said.
